findings.description: The audit_trail bucket sets acl = "lcatalogopts-delivery-write", an invalid/foreign canned ACL value rather than "private". If the provider normalizes it (historically AWS treated unrecognized canned ACLs as public-read), the audit bucket storing log data becomes readable by the public, exposing audit records.
reports_archive has no server_side_encryption_configuration and no default encryption, so objects (including the vendor-roster spreadsheet seeded into it) are stored unencrypted at rest.
ledger_exports holds financial ledger exports but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
model_artifacts has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
ops_runbooks stores operational runbooks without any server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving its contents unencrypted at rest.
reports_archive has neither versioning nor access logging configured, unlike the other buckets, so object overwrites/deletions and access to archived reports are not recoverable or auditable.
